## codegraph
# Codegraph — code intelligence over an indexed knowledge graph

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of every symbol, edge, and file in
the workspace — pre-computed structure you would otherwise re-derive by
reading files (cached intelligence: thousands of parse/trace decisions you
don't pay to re-reason each run). Reads are sub-millisecond; the index lags
writes by ~1s through the file watcher. Reach for it BEFORE *and* while
writing or editing code — not just for questions: one call returns the
verbatim source PLUS who calls it and what it affects, so you edit with the
blast radius in view. More accurate context, in far fewer tokens and
round-trips than reading files yourself.

## One tool: codegraph_explore — use it instead of reading files

There is a single tool, `codegraph_explore`, and it is Read-equivalent. It
takes either a natural-language question or a bag of symbol/file names and
returns the **verbatim, line-numbered source** of the relevant symbols
grouped by file — the same `<n>\t<line>` shape `Read` gives you, safe to
`Edit` from — PLUS the call path among them (including dynamic-dispatch hops
like callbacks, React re-render, and JSX children that grep can't follow) and
a blast-radius summary of what depends on them.

Whether you're answering "how does X work" or implementing a change (fixing a
bug, adding a feature), call `codegraph_explore` before you Read. ONE call
usually answers the whole question. Codegraph IS the pre-built search index —
so running your own grep + read loop, or delegating the lookup to a separate
file-reading sub-task/agent, repeats work codegraph already did and costs more
for the same answer. A direct codegraph answer is typically one to a few
calls; a grep/read exploration is dozens.

## How to query

- **Almost any question — "how does X work", architecture, a bug, "what/where is X", or surveying an area** → `codegraph_explore` with a natural-language question or the relevant names. ONE capped call returns the verbatim source grouped by file; most often the ONLY call y… [truncated]

74			}

87					// The expiration time is set to 5 days.
88					if time.Now().Before(s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime.AsTime().Add(4 * 24 * time.Hour)) {
89						continue
90					}
91				}
92	
93				s3Config := instanceStorageSetting.GetS3Config()
94				if s3ObjectPayload.S3Config != nil {

106				}

94

97		}
98

100		defer s.jobsMu.RUnlock()

110			rj.cancelFn = cancel

121	func (s *Scheduler) runJobWithSchedule(ctx context.Context, rj *registeredJob, schedule *Schedule) {
122		defer s.wg.Done()

124		// Apply middleware to handler
125		handler := rj.job.Handler
126		if s.middleware != nil {
127			handler = s.middleware(handler)
128		}
129	
130		for {
131			// Calculate next run time
132			now := time.Now()
133			if rj.job.Timezone != "" {
134				loc, err := time.LoadLocation(rj.job.Timezone)
135				if err == nil {
136					now = now.In(loc)
137				}
138			} else if s.timezone != nil {
139				now = now.In(s.timezone)
140			}
141	
142			next := schedule.Next(now)
143			duration := time.Until(next)
144	
145			timer := time.NewTimer(duration)
146	
147			select {
148			case <-timer.C:
149				// Add job name to context and execute
150				jobCtx := withJobName(ctx, rj.job.Name)
151				if err := handler(jobCtx); err != nil {
152					// Error already handled by middleware (if any)
153					_ = err
154				}
155			case <-ctx.Done():
156				// Stop the timer to prevent it from firing. The timer will be garbage collected.
157				timer.Stop()
158				return
159			case <-s.stopCh:
160				// Stop the timer to prevent it from firing. The timer will be garbage collected.
161				timer.Stop()

163			}

167	// Stop gracefully shuts down the scheduler.
168	// It waits for all running jobs to complete or until the context is canceled.
169	func (s *Scheduler) Stop(ctx context.Context) error {
170		s.runningMu.Lock()
171		if !s.running {
172			s.runningMu.Unlock()
173			return errors.New("scheduler not running")
174		}
175		s.running = false
176		s.runningMu.Unlock()
177	
178		// Cancel all job contexts
179		s.jobsMu.RLock()
180		for _, rj := range s.jobs {
181			if rj.cancelFn != nil {
182				rj.cancelFn()
183			}
184		}
185		s.jobsMu.RUnlock()
186	
187		// Signal stop and wait for jobs to finish
188		close(s.stopCh)
189	
190		done := make(chan struct{})
191		go func() {
192			s.wg.Wait()
193			close(done)
194		}()
195	
196		select {
197		case <-done:
198			return nil
199		case <-ctx.Done():
200			return ctx.Err()
201		}

154		// Create a separate context for each background runner

192		case <-done:
193		case <-ctx.Done():

195			case <-done:
196				return

198			}

52	}

60	}

64		return &SSEHub{

70	// The caller must call Unsubscribe when done.
71	func (h *SSEHub) Subscribe(userID int32, role store.Role) *SSEClient {
72		c := &SSEClient{
73			// Buffer a few events so a slow client doesn't block broadcasting.
74			events: make(chan []byte, 32),
75			userID: userID,
76			role:   role,
77		}
78		h.mu.Lock()
79		if h.closed {
80			close(c.events)
81		} else {

83		}
84		h.mu.Unlock()
85		return c

90		h.mu.Lock()

92			delete(h.clients, c)
93			close(c.events)

95		h.mu.Unlock()

	markdownService := markdown.NewService(

content.text:
h15.

- **`checkMemoReadAccess`** — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39-68` — gates single-memo reads (used by `GetMemo` at `memo_service.go:356,367` and `ListMemoComments` at `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:148`), denying non-public/archived memos to anyone but the creator.
- **`ListMemos` visibility filter** — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:219,225` — restricts the query's `VisibilityList` to `[Public]` for unauthenticated callers or `[Public, Protected]` for authenticated non-owners before hitting the store.
- **Memo comment creation check** — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41` — rejects creating a comment on a `Private` memo unless the requester is the memo's creator or a super user.
- **RSS feed generation** — `server/router/rss/rss.go:90,141` — hard-restricts feed queries to `VisibilityList: [store.Public]`, so protected/private memos never appear in RSS output.
- **Attachment/file server** — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:677,699` — checks the owning memo's `Visibility` before streaming attachment bytes: public content requires `AllowAnonymous`, and private content requires the requester to be the creator or an admin.

cacheConfig := cache.Config{

    MaxItems:        1000,
    OnEviction:      nil,
}

**Premise correction:** Neither NATS nor RabbitMQ (nor any external message broker) is used — a repo-wide search finds no imports or references to `nats`, `rabbitmq`, `amqp`, or any message-queue client library in the codebase.

**Actual mechanism:** Webhook delivery workers consume from an in-process, in-memory Go channel, not a broker. It's declared in `internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`:

```go
asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)
```

Four goroutines are spawned in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`) that range over `asyncPostQueue` and call `Post` for each payload. Producers enqueue via `PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184-196`), which does a non-blocking `select` send to `asyncPostQueue` and drops (logging a warning) if the buffered channel (capacity 128) is full — there's no persistence, acknowledgement, or external broker involved, just an in-memory bounded queue local to the running server process.

**Premise correction:** There is no GraphQL schema anywhere in this repository — a search for `graphql`/`GraphQL` across the codebase returns zero hits.

**Actual API surface:** The public API is defined as **Protocol Buffers (gRPC) service definitions** under `proto/api/v1/` — e.g. `memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, plus shared types in `common.proto`. These are compiled to Go bindings under `proto/gen/api/v1/` (gRPC server/client stubs, e.g. `proto/gen/api/v1/user_service_grpc.pb.go`) and exposed over HTTP via a gRPC-Gateway/Connect layer (`proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/`, `*.pb.gw.go` files), registered in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go`. There's also a separate MCP (Model Context Protocol) surface with an OpenAPI-derived schema layer under `server/router/mcp/` (`openapi.go`, `catalog.go`), but that's OpenAPI/JSON-schema-based tool definitions for MCP, not GraphQL.
